The business is anchored by AAON Oklahoma, which generated about US$1.1b of revenue, with AAON Coil Products at roughly US$461 million and BasX at about US$535 million, partly offset by US$199 million of eliminations between segments. Investors watching the AI data center freight story may want AAON on their radar because BasX branded data center solutions and high efficiency rooftop units are tied directly to the heavy HVAC boxes that fill those new server halls, feeding ongoing trucking needs while projects are built out. The company has pointed to a sizable backlog, new capacity in Memphis and interest in liquid and air side cooling for denser AI facilities. These factors together could support future earnings if orders flow through cleanly. At the same time, AAON is working through ERP and capacity ramp issues, carries meaningful capital spending and has seen margins under pressure, so any stumble in execution or a pause in data center build plans could have a negative impact. For investors comfortable with that trade off, AAON offers a focused way to follow how AI driven cooling demand and construction freight translate into future cash and earnings quality.

The business is split between Systems Protection, which generated about US$3.4b of revenue, and Electrical Connections at roughly US$1.4b. Investors watching the AI data center freight theme may find nVent Electric hard to ignore because it sells the physical gear that goes onto flatbeds, into modular outdoor enclosures and across rural job sites as power hungry facilities are built out. Management has talked about record orders, a growing backlog and new liquid cooling capacity that tie directly to data center projects.
